hypotheses.title: Possible relationship between Amiga CPIC1 blocks 1 and 129
hypotheses.relationHypothesis: A user suggested block 1 may show a Bazz/Baaz Draconian standing, block 129 may show an attack, and another image may be used during movement. This subject and frame-role interpretation is unverified.

evidence.reference: conversation:Champions of Krynn (Amiga) CPIC1 block 129 discussion
evidence.note: User's original wording: ‘Nu er det f.eks. en Bazz Draconian hvis jeg husker rigtigt, og det er hvor den angriber imens block 1 er hvor den står uden at angribe, og den som bliver brugt når den bevæger sig f.eks.’ This is a lead for review, not verified game evidence.

The private Amiga disk1/game and disk2/CPIC1.DAA files are present and match recorded SHA-256 pins; this establishes source availability only, not their CPIC1 selector, consumer or shared installation.
Both source records have pinned decoded pixel hashes and visual descriptions. Their visual appearance differs; these facts do not establish a shared subject, animation, or game use.

limits: No verified Amiga runtime selector/load trace establishes when either source is used.
No movement frame has been identified.
The pinned Amiga executable and CPIC1 archive are locally present, but a CPIC1-specific selector/load/draw trace establishing subject identity and playback is not yet recorded.
No reusable, reviewed HUNK/relocation parser was located in checked-in tools for continuing the static executable trace.
Do not add these sources to an animation group or imply playback order or timing from this hypothesis.
